title: Analog Design
intro: A structured course on analog CMOS integrated-circuit design, built to be learned in order: each chapter uses the ideas of the ones before it.

items: Read each page in order within a chapter; the chapter page lists what its subtopics cover.
Run the interactive simulations and change one parameter at a time, predicting the result first.
Try every Problem before opening its hidden solution (click 'Show hint' or 'Show solution'). The answer line at the end is the quick check.
Highlight any term to see its definition.
Introduction to Analog Design: Why analog still matters, why integrated, why CMOS, and the levels of abstraction.
Basic MOS Device Physics: Structure, I/V characteristics, second-order effects and small-signal models.
Single-Stage Amplifiers: The basic building blocks: CS, source follower, CG and cascode.
Differential Amplifiers: Differential versus single-ended signalling, the differential pair, common-mode response and loads.
Current Mirrors and Biasing: Basic, cascode and active current mirrors, and biasing techniques.
Frequency Response of Amplifiers: Miller effect, poles and zeros, speed of each stage and gain-bandwidth trade-offs.
Noise: Noise types, representation in circuits, and noise in amplifiers.
Feedback: Feedback properties, topologies, loading and Bode's analysis.
Operational Amplifiers: Performance, one-stage and two-stage op amps, gain boosting, CMFB, slew rate, PSRR and noise.
Stability and Frequency Compensation: Phase margin, compensating single- and two-stage op amps.
Nanometer Design Studies: Designing amplifiers with short-channel transistors.
Bandgap References: Supply- and temperature-independent voltage references.
Switched-Capacitor Circuits: Sampling switches, SC amplifiers and integrators.
Nonlinearity and Mismatch: Distortion and random variation limits.
Oscillators: Ring and LC oscillators and VCOs.
Phase-Locked Loops: Phase detectors, charge pumps, loop dynamics and DLLs.
Short-Channel Effects and Device Models: Scaling, short-channel behaviour and corners.
CMOS Processing Technology: How CMOS chips are made.
Layout and Packaging: Analog layout and packaging parasitics.

blocks.text: Basic circuit analysis (Kirchhoff's laws, Thevenin/Norton, small-signal AC analysis) and a little semiconductor physics. Equations on these pages are written in plain text: gm is transconductance, ro output resistance, Vov overdrive voltage, || means parallel.

The structure and examples follow the standard treatment in B. Razavi, Design of Analog CMOS Integrated Circuits (2nd ed.), with additional explanations, simulations and practice problems written for this library. Numbers in the problems are chosen to be easy to check by hand, not to represent a specific process.
